newsitem.title: FRANCE: WEU expects pact on using ex-Soviet planes in crises.
newsitem.headline: WEU expects pact on using ex-Soviet planes in crises.

text.p: PARIS, May 13, Reuter - The Western European Union will sign accords soon with Russia and Ukraine to fly European troops to crisis zones aboard former Soviet transports, a senior European officer said on Tuesday.
"We expect these accords with Moscow and Kiev to be signed in a matter of weeks," the officer told Reuters.
He was speaking at a ministerial meeting of WEU, a European defence grouping without heavy airlift capacity.
The WEU wants to show Europe can undertake long-range military interventions when the U.S.-led NATO alliance, to which most WEU states belong, does not want to get involved.

"As you know, we have been negotiating with the United States for years for the placing at Europe's disposal of NATO assets such as American heavy-lift transport planes when the need arises," the officer said.

"However we must face reality and in some combat operations, we have to take into account that (the U.S.) Congress may veto even the simple backing of transport aircraft if its means U.S. personnel might be endangered.
"As an alternative, we therefore started looking towards Russia and Ukraine who also have heavy-lift transport planes and who need the cash," the officer said.

During the Cold War in the mid-1970s, Washington rushed giant cargo planes to France to pick up French troops destined for Zaire where they prevented Cuban-backed rebels from overthrowing President Mobutu Sese Seko.
France now regularly charters Ukrainian Antonov 124 transports to fly armoured cars and helicopter gunships to crises in Africa.

The WEU officer said a framework agreement between WEU and Russia and Ukraine would set in advance prices for such flights for European operations and put them under supervision of Russian and Ukrainian authorities.
This would theoretically ensure availability of the planes and exclude sudden price rises in crunch times.
"It would also be a nice diplomatic signal that the European countries want good relations with the former Eastern bloc states," the officer said.
A final declaration at the WEU ministerial meeting said:
"Russia and Ukraine play an essential role in Europe's security and stability. WEU has demonstrated its concern to consolidate and develop harmonious relations with these two countries."
The document said WEU welcomed the start of talks with Moscow and Kiev on "making strategic air transport assets available" but gave no time frame for the plan.

The WEU, which France and Germany would like to see become the "European pillar" of NATO, has long been negotiating with the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation for the loan of its "assets" including aircraft.
But Washington has made clear it wished to keep strict control over the use of U.S. equipment and personnel when loaned.
European planners want to avoid American meddling in their control over operations and the possible accord with Russia and Ukraine would presumably make this possible.
